en.title: Minimum Total Price to Buy a Given Number of Items From Infinite Arithmetic Price Lists
en.description:
In category i, the j-th item costs a[i]+(j−1)b[i], and every category has infinitely many items. Buy exactly m items and minimize the total price.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; additions for bounds missing from the sources and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by one line of n values a and one line of n values b. The original bounds are 1≤n,m≤100000, 1≤a[i],b[i]≤100000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 7; 21; and 6, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: A min-heap holds the cheapest unbought item of each category. Each time, pop the minimum price, add it to the total, and push the next price from the same category; repeat m times.
